connect.description: Use the model loaded in Temper from coding agents, editors and your own code through OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs.
connect.no_model: No model is loaded. Requests that name a downloaded model load it while loading on demand is on; others fail until you load one on the Models page.
connect.tip: The key stays the same when Temper restarts, so these configs keep working. From a terminal, {start} (or {codex}, {opencode}, {aider}) starts the agent already pointed at the loaded model. Claude Code reads a long system prompt and many tool descriptions, so load the model with a context of 32K or more, and pick one that's good at calling tools.
connect.other_apps_hint: Many apps look for a local model at Ollama's or llama.cpp's usual address. Temper can answer there too, on this computer only. Like Ollama, those addresses take no key.
connect.other_devices_hint: Let phones and other computers on your home network use the loaded model.
connect.linked_hint: Use another computer's models from this one, such as a desktop's GPU from a laptop. On that computer, turn on serving on the network and make an API key, then link it here. Ask for its models as {name}; a model only it has can be asked for by name alone. The preferred device answers for models both computers have.
connect.decisions_hint: Typed answers for your apps: yes or no, one of a set, labels or a score, each with a reason. Save a question by name and an app sends only the text, to {path}. The loaded model answers, or a classifier you trained on the Train page.
connect.api_keys_hint: Give each app or device its own key instead of Temper's, so you can see what each one uses and revoke it on its own. These keys open the model API ({path}) and nothing else.

connect.mcp_tip: Or, from a terminal: {add} (or {codex}, {cursor}, {vscode}) adds it for you, and {doctor} checks it.

train.o_sft_note: Learns to write the replies in the data.
train.o_dpo_note: Learns which of two replies is better, from rows with a prompt, a chosen and a rejected reply. Stays close to the starting model.
train.o_orpo_note: Fine-tunes on the chosen replies while pushing away from the rejected ones, in one step. Same rows as DPO.
train.o_simpo_note: Compares the two replies' average likelihood, with a margin. Same rows as DPO; uses less memory.
train.o_grpo_note: Writes several replies to each prompt, scores them with your rewards, and favours the ones that beat their group. Rows need a prompt, and usually the expected answer.
train.o_dr_grpo_note: GRPO without its bias towards long wrong replies and easy questions. Same rows and rewards.
train.o_dapo_note: GRPO that weighs every token equally, so long replies count fully, and skips prompts whose replies all scored the same.
train.o_kto_note: Learns from single replies marked good or bad (rows with a prompt, a completion and a true or false label), so no pairs are needed. Pairs work too.
train.m_qlora_note: 4-bit base weights plus small adapters. Uses the least memory.
train.m_lora_note: 16-bit base weights plus adapters. Slightly better quality, about twice the memory.
train.m_full_note: Updates every weight. Needs a large GPU, or on a Mac a 16-bit model and plenty of memory.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.about: Temper sends no telemetry: no usage data, no analytics, nothing about your chats, models or files. It goes online only to do what you ask, like downloading a model or searching the web, and to check for updates (which you can turn off above). The libraries it uses are told not to send telemetry either.
privacy.offer_hint: When Temper hits an error, it saves a report here, without your home folder, keys or tokens. With this on, it also offers to open it as a GitHub issue, which you read and send yourself.

attach.too_big: {name} may not fit in the model's {n}-token context.
stats.title: Statistics
stats.counted: Counted on this computer, from replies through Temper's model API, its own chats included. None of it is sent anywhere.
stats.counted_since: Counted on this computer since {date}, from replies through Temper's model API, its own chats included. None of it is sent anywhere.
queue.waiting: {n} queued, sent when the reply finishes
queue.move: Move queued message {n}. Drag, or use the arrow keys.
hub.about_mirror: Same models and names as Hugging Face, through a mirror such as hf-mirror.com or one your company runs. Training and export use it too. If you've added a Hugging Face token, it's sent to the mirror, so only use mirrors you trust.
hub.about_ms: ModelScope hosts most popular models, often under the publisher's name. Downloads go into the same library, so chat and training work as usual. Gated models and datasets still come from Hugging Face; local dataset files always work.
hub.title: Model source
eng.about_llamacpp: Runs GGUF models on any computer. Chat's default.
eng.about_mlx: Runs MLX and Hugging Face model folders on Apple Silicon, and fine-tunes from this Mac before exporting.
eng.about_transformers: Runs Hugging Face model folders with PyTorch. Slower, but takes almost any model.
eng.about_gpu: Fast serving on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs; splits big models across several GPUs.
eng.remove_confirm: Remove {name}? Its environment is deleted; you can install it again later.
eng.title: Inference engines
eng.load_hint: Hugging Face and MLX model folders get a Load button on the Models page once an engine that runs them is ready.
eng.unload_hint: Frees their memory. Several models can be loaded at once with Alongside on the Models page.
diag.title: Diagnostics
diag.about: Checks drivers, GPU libraries, disk space, the API port and the engine's packages, and says how to fix what it finds.
diag.not_ready: Diagnostics run once the engine is ready.
presets.label: Settings preset
presets.save_title: Save these settings as a preset
presets.stop_default: Stop using this preset when this model loads
presets.make_default: Use this preset whenever this model loads
presets.name: Preset name
presets.saves: Saves the system prompt, sampling, max tokens and thinking choices.
lic.title: Open-source licences
lic.about: Temper is licensed under Apache-2.0 and includes the open-source software below.
lic.downloaded_hint: First-run setup and the Models page install these from their publishers. They run under their own licences, and Temper does not modify them.
storage.title: Storage
storage.bar: Temper uses {size}; {free} of the disk is free
storage.stay: Models already downloaded stay where they are and won't show in Temper until you switch back.
storage.moving: Moving models… Chat and downloads can wait until this finishes.
storage.back: Go back to the standard folder
storage.shared: The standard folder is shared with other Hugging Face tools. Another folder is used only by Temper.
storage.move_failed: Moving the models stopped: {error}. Models moved so far are in the new folder; the rest are where they were.
cat.add_training: Add training support in Settings to fine-tune.
cat.unsupported: The trainer Temper installed doesn't support this model's architecture yet.
cat.gated: Accept the licence on Hugging Face first
cat.moe_title: Mixture of experts: only part of the model runs for each token, so it's faster than its size suggests.
cat.fit_title: About {gb} GB for a 4-bit file with an 8K context
cat.recommends: {publisher} recommends {settings}. Chat uses these when you load it.
cat.no_settings: {publisher} doesn't publish recommended settings; chat keeps its defaults.
cat.about: Models we recommend, with the settings their publishers suggest. The fit is for a 4-bit file with an 8K context; open a model to see every size of file.
hf.title: Hugging Face account
hf.start_engine: Start the engine to manage your token.
hf.keychain: Token saved in your system keychain.
hf.session: Token set for this engine session.
hf.cli: Using the token from huggingface-cli login.
hf.invalid: The saved token no longer works. Add a new one.
hf.none: No token. Public models download without one; gated models such as Llama and Gemma need it.
hf.create: Create a read token on Hugging Face
setup.title: Set up Temper
setup.about: Temper keeps its engine, Python and the packages that run models, in its own folder. Nothing else on your computer changes.
setup.fix: Fix the problem below and try again. Anything already downloaded is reused.
setup.heavy: This downloads about 6 GB of GPU libraries, so it can take a while.
setup.quick: This takes a minute or two on a typical connection.
speech.failed: It failed; the log says why.
speech.remove_confirm: Remove speech to text? Its environment is deleted; downloaded models stay.
speech.title: Speech to text
speech.about: Dictate in Chat with the microphone button, and transcribe recordings into text and subtitles. Whisper runs on this computer; nothing is sent anywhere. Apps can use it at {path}.
speech.path: Path to an audio or video file
speech.saved: Saved as text, SRT and WebVTT subtitles, and JSON.
speech.saved_lang: Saved as text, SRT and WebVTT subtitles, and JSON ({language}).
ms.running_on_adapter: Running on {engine}, with the fine-tuned adapter on top.
ms.context_hint: How much of the chat the model can see at once. Longer needs more memory.
ms.kv_needs_flash: A quantized cache needs flash attention.
ms.kv_hint: The memory that holds the context.
ms.tp_hint: GPUs each layer is split across.
ms.pp_hint: Groups of layers on separate GPUs.
ms.cpu_hint: Layers left on the CPU free GPU memory but run slower.
ms.spec_hint: Drafts tokens ahead so the model checks several at once. Replies are the same, often faster.
ms.no_draft: No draft model here shares this model's tokenizer. A small model from the same family (for example its 0.6B or 1B size) can draft for it.
ms.last_spec: Last reply: {speed} tokens/s, {pct}% of {n} drafted tokens accepted.
ms.few_accepted: So few are accepted that drafting likely slows replies; try fewer tokens at a time, prompt lookup, or Off.
ms.needs: Needs about {size} of the {budget} this computer can give it.
